scope: Local SQL014 exact onboarding.submit replay authorizes against immutable submitted version, not a later mutable draft

nativePostgres.scenario: After submitting A, requesting changes, and saving B, exact replay returns the original receipt; pg_blocking_pids confirms revoking A waits for replay to commit; revocation then succeeds and subsequent replay returns 42501. B remains active and one immutable A version/receipt remain.

behavior.receiptVersion: Resolve requestId and revision from the exact receipt; load onboarding_request_versions for that organization/request/revision and require submitted_by=actor.
behavior.authorization: For replay, check company/team membership from the immutable submitted payload. Do not validate or authorize against a later draft, and do not revalidate mutable catalogue eligibility.
behavior.locking: Include membership:<company>:<actor> identities from the selected payload in the ordered advisory lock scopes before FOR SHARE membership checks; exact receipt path writes no command, operation, or membership fence.

limitations: Synthetic local data only; SQL014 was not applied remotely.
The native PostgreSQL runner covers replay-first serialization and then A revocation; inverse membership and empty-later-draft cases are in PGlite only.
This fix covers exact onboarding.submit replay only; it does not close remaining M2.2C/Gate L families.
